charts.title: Missing activation prerequisites
charts.subtitle: Each restaurant lacks realtime enablement, a registered printer, and an assigned print route.

blocks.body:
# Print Agent: Five-Day Health Check

**Window:** October 3–7, 2026 through 10:35 PKT.

## Executive Summary

- **No live benefit was recorded.** The configured RMS database has zero print jobs in the five-day window and zero print jobs across all history.
- **Realtime printing is not active.** All three restaurants have realtime printing disabled, no registered printers, and no print routes.
- **The implementation passes its automated checks.** All four WebSocket tests passed, covering signed tokens, agent generation, tenant/printer isolation, PostgreSQL notifications, and atomic claiming.
- **Verdict: technically ready, operationally unproven.** There is no evidence that WebSocket printing is failing, but there is also no live usage from which to measure speed or reliability.

## The system has not processed any print workload

There were no sales, printers, or print jobs for any configured restaurant during the reporting window. Success rate and latency are therefore **undefined**, not 0%. The environment has received no measurable benefit from WebSocket printing because the feature has not been enabled or exercised.

## The WebSocket design has a resilient fallback

When enabled, PostgreSQL queue notifications trigger printer-specific Socket.IO events for immediate pickup. A five-second reconciliation poll remains active to recover missed events or work through proxies that block WebSockets.

Expected benefits are faster pickup, fewer empty polling requests, and tenant/printer isolation. The current schema does not persist whether a claim came from WebSocket or reconciliation polling, so those benefits cannot be quantified retrospectively.

## Recommended next steps

1. Register a physical printer for one test restaurant.
2. Configure a customer, unpaid-bill, or kitchen printer route.
3. Enable realtime printing and install the generated realtime agent.
4. Run controlled orders and verify the queue reaches `printed`.
5. Record connection uptime, notification time, claim source, claim latency, retries, and confirmation latency.

## Further questions

- Is this configured database production, staging, or development?
- Which restaurant and printer should be used for the controlled trial?
- Should the service target be 99% successful printing and 95% claimed within two seconds?

## Caveats and assumptions

- Asia/Karachi time is used; October 7 is a partial day through 10:35 PKT.
- Findings apply only to the database configured by this workspace.
- Zero sales means the lack of print jobs is consistent with no transaction demand, not necessarily a malfunction.
- No chart is shown because every observed operational value is zero; a chart would imply a trend that the data cannot support.

query.description: Checks realtime settings, printer registration, sales activity, and print jobs for all restaurants.
query.sql: SELECT s.name, s.realtime_printing_enabled, COUNT(DISTINCT p.id) AS printers, COUNT(DISTINCT sa.id) AS sales, COUNT(DISTINCT pq.id) AS print_jobs FROM shops s LEFT JOIN printers p ON p.shop_id=s.id LEFT JOIN sales sa ON sa.shop_id=s.id AND sa.created_at >= TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-10-02 19:00:00+00' AND sa.created_at < TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-10-07 19:00:00+00' LEFT JOIN print_queue pq ON pq.shop_id=s.id AND pq.created_at >= TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-10-02 19:00:00+00' AND pq.created_at < TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-10-07 19:00:00+00' GROUP BY s.id, s.name, s.realtime_printing_enabled ORDER BY s.name;

document.title: Realtime Print Agent automated tests
document.description: Four passing tests covering token security, generated agent separation, shop/printer event isolation, and atomic PostgreSQL queue claiming.
